Thanks for flagging, Mateo—quick read below (high-level, will follow with annotated doc by EOD Mon):

Summary of priorities I see now:
- SCCs references: HealthBridge used the EU Commission's 2024 SCCs template and linked it into the DPA. That part is fine; the friction point is their attempt to require Redwood to be named as a "data importer" and accept a broader liability carve-in in clause 7.2.
- KMS requirement (4.2): acceptable as an opt-in addendum for Private deployments but cannot be a mandatory term for Hosted (we do not provide customer-managed HSM for hosted API). Suggest: make KMS clause conditional and add a short scoping sentence tying it to "Private Deployment Appendix".
- Delegation/processor roles: they ask for processor-to-processor delegation visibility and details on subprocessor list cadence. Our standard approach is to publish subprocessor list with 30 days' notice and include annual certification. They asked for immediate on-boarding evidence (SOC 2 extract). We can offer the SOC 2 extract and KMS architecture diagram as evidence but must avoid operational SOP commitments in the contract.

Immediate asks for HealthBridge legal-to-legal call:
- Confirm that KMS will be limited to Private deployment customers and specify the clause change (I can propose language).
- Push back on the unlimited liability wording in clause 7.2 — propose a liability cap tied to annual contract value or carve out specific categories.
- Agree on evidence delivery timeline: SOC 2 + subprocessor list in 5 business days once contract signed; architecture diagram upon NDA.

I'll produce an annotated redline (track suggested edits) and drop it here by Mon 17:00 PT. Mateo — please include any commercial guardrails Ben thinks are relevant.

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
